items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: you learned from records and all that, Henderson's band and Trumbower and whatever

ctx.x: I guess -- you know, you saying that
you learned from records and all that, Henderson's band and Trumbower and whatever, so once records came in and people were able to buy records --

Right. And then you learn from each other as you went, and those same guys had to learn from listening to records. So everybody learned from each other. And that's the way the whole thing did. But I think the critics and a lot of people that weren't musicians, that write the books and things, they put these cliches on jazz and bebop and all that. It's just the evolution of jazz and the thing just kept on evolving from the way I used to play it by ear until the way -- then I began to learn about chords and harmony…
